Icon Mapping

Source: R/scales.R
icon-scales.Rd

Conveniently maps data values to icons for use in magicIcons(). These functions mirror leaflet::colorFactor(), leaflet::colorBin() and leaflet::colorQuantile(): given the same domain, levels, bins, pretty, n, probs, reverse and right arguments, an icon function and a colour function will split the data in exactly the same way. If icons and palette have the same length (one per level/bin), each level therefore receives a unique and consistent icon-colour pair. Icons are, by their nature, discrete, so there is no analogue to leaflet::colorNumeric(). For iconBin() and iconQuantile(), it makes sense to pick "ordered" icons such as the "hourglass" or "temperature" icon families in Font Awesome.

Usage

iconFactor(
  icons,
  domain,
  levels = NULL,
  ordered = FALSE,
  na.icon = "auto",
  reverse = FALSE
)

iconBin(
  icons,
  domain,
  bins = length(icons),
  pretty = TRUE,
  na.icon = "auto",
  reverse = FALSE,
  right = FALSE
)

iconQuantile(
  icons,
  domain,
  n = length(icons),
  probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n + 1),
  na.icon = "auto",
  reverse = FALSE,
  right = FALSE
)

Arguments

icons

The icons that values will be mapped to, one per level or bin. Icons may be repeated. Note that the library (e.g., "fontawesome") is defined in magicIcons().

domain

The possible values that can be mapped. For iconFactor() this should be categorical data (character or factor). For iconBin() and iconQuantile() this should be numeric. If NULL, levels/bins are calculated from the data each time the function is called, as in {leaflet}.

levels

An alternate way of specifying levels; if specified, domain is ignored.

ordered

If TRUE and domain needs to be coerced to a factor, treat it as already in the correct order.

na.icon

The icon to return for missing or out-of-scope values. The default, "auto", is drawn by magicIcons() and addIconLegend() as a question mark from whichever library they use. If the scale maps values to marker shapes instead, "auto" is drawn as "none" (the icon alone). NA draws no icon (or, for shapes, no marker) and leaves missing values out of legends.

reverse

If TRUE, the order of icons is reversed.

bins

Either a numeric vector of two or more unique cut points or a single number (greater than or equal to 2) giving the number of intervals into which the domain values are to be cut. Defaults to length(icons).

pretty

Whether to use the function pretty() to generate the bins when bins is a single number. Note that when pretty = TRUE, the number of bins may not equal bins, and may therefore not equal the number of icons; a warning is given if so. Use pretty = FALSE to guarantee one bin per icon.

right

Should the intervals be closed on the right (and open on the left)? Passed to cut(). Note that, to match leaflet::colorQuantile(), right is ignored by iconQuantile() when domain is not NULL.

n

Number of equal-size quantiles desired. For more precise control, use the probs argument instead. Defaults to length(icons).

probs

A more precise alternative to n. Passed directly to stats::quantile().

Value

A function that takes a single parameter, x; when called with a vector of factors/characters (for iconFactor()) or numbers (for iconBin() and iconQuantile()), icon names are returned.

Matching icons to levels

Levels are ordered in the same way as leaflet::colorFactor(): factor levels if domain is a factor, the order of appearance if ordered = TRUE, and otherwise sorted alphabetically. For iconBin() and iconQuantile(), bins are ordered from lowest to highest. The first icon is assigned to the first level, the second to the second, and so on.

Colour palettes can interpolate between colours when there are more levels than colours; icons cannot. If the number of icons differs from the number of levels/bins, each level is given the icon at the equivalent position along the list of icons (so some icons may be repeated or skipped) and a warning is issued.

Examples

types <- c("Urban Traffic", "Urban Industrial", "Urban Background")

# levels are sorted, as in leaflet::colorFactor()
iconPal <- iconFactor(c("house", "industry", "car"), types)
colorPal <- leaflet::colorFactor(c("#28A197", "#12436D", "#801650"), types)
data.frame(type = types, icon = iconPal(types), color = colorPal(types))
#>               type     icon   color
#> 1    Urban Traffic      car #801650
#> 2 Urban Industrial industry #12436D
#> 3 Urban Background    house #28A197

# numeric data
binPal <- iconBin(
  c("temperature-low", "temperature-half", "temperature-high"),
  domain = 0:30
)
binPal(c(2, 15, 28))
#> [1] "temperature-low"  "temperature-half" "temperature-high"
